metas.name: Albania - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Albanian chevrons are white on black.

--- NOTE:

  • Within southern Europe this chevron is also used by Italy, Greece, and Spain.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/albania.

metas.name: Argentina - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Argentina typically uses white-and-red chevrons.

--- NOTE:

  • Argentina is the only American country with these chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Australia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Australia uses white on black chevrons.
  • They also use black on yellow chevrons but are much rarer.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Austria - Chevrons
metas.note:
Austria uses two colour schemes for chevrons:

  • White on red
  • Red on yellow

--- NOTE:

  • Germany mostly uses red on white chevrons, and rarely red on yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/austria.

metas.name: Azores - Chevrons
metas.note: • Since the Azores is an autonomous region of Portugal, you will often come across various types of Portuguese infrastructure, such as poles, chevrons and bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Belgium - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Belgium uses white chevrons, with a red arrow.

--- NOTE:

  • The Netherlands also uses this chevron.
  • You will not see these in France.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/belgium.

metas.name: Botswana - Chevrons
metas.note:
• These small red-and-white chevrons can sometimes be found next to the road.

--- NOTE:

  • They are also very common in South Africa.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Brazil - Chevrons
metas.note: • Brazil uses yellow on black chevrons, as opposed to most of South America, which use black on yellow chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Bulgarian chevrons are typically red on white.

--- NOTE:

  • Many other European countries have similar chevrons.
  • Crucially, among neighbouring countries, Romania, Turkey, and North Macedonia use the same chevrons.
  • Greece and Serbia use black and white chevrons however.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bulgaria.

metas.name: Cambodia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Chevrons in Cambodia are black with yellow arrows.
  • Chevrons are somewhat rare.

--- NOTE:

Chevrons in all other Southeast Asian countries have the reverse colour scheme:

  • Yellow with black arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Croatia - Chevrons
metas.note: • Croatia features chevrons with a red arrow on a yellow or white background.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Czechia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Czech and Slovak chevrons are white with red arrows.
  • Less commonly, you may find red on yellow chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Denmark - Chevrons
metas.note:
• This red-and-white chevron is found in Denmark.
  • They are often low to the ground.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Ecuador - Chevron Spam
metas.note:
• Ecuador often uses a lot of chevrons in road curves (“chevron spam”), usually considerably more than most other Latin American countries.

--- NOTE:

  • Colombia also occasionally uses a lot of chevrons in curves.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Estonia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Estonia uses red chevrons with white arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Russia and Ukraine use the same chevrons.

However, Latvian and Lithuanian chevrons have the opposite colour scheme:

  • White with red arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/estonia.

metas.name: Finland - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Finnish chevrons are black with yellow arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Norway and Iceland have similarly coloured chevrons.
  • Sweden, on the other hand, has unique blue and yellow chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/finland.

metas.name: France - Chevrons
metas.note:
• France uses chevrons with white arrows on a blue background.
  • They can have a wide amount of arrows, ranging from one to five.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other European country with this colour scheme is Spain, where you will only find chevrons with two or four arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: Greece - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Greek chevrons have white arrows on a black background.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar chevrons are found in Albania, Italy and the UK.
  • Spain has the same colours, but will almost always have either two or four arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Hungary - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Hungarian chevrons are white on red.
  • Black-and-white chevrons may also be seen, but are considerably less common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/hungary.

metas.name: Iceland - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Icelandic chevrons are black with yellow arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Norway and Finland have similarly coloured chevrons.
  • Sweden, on the other hand, has unique blue and yellow chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: Ireland - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Irish chevrons are yellow on black.
  • Both single and multiple arrows are common.

--- NOTE:

  • UK chevrons are white on black.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Israel - Chevrons
metas.note: • Chevrons are white on black.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Italy - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Italian chevrons are white arrows on a black background.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southern Europe, white on black chevrons can also be found in Spain, Greece and Albania.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Jersey - Chevrons
metas.note:
• In general, road infrastructure is similar to that found in the United Kingdom.
  • This includes driving on the left, as well as directional signs, chevrons and warning signs.
  • Chevrons often have a big yellow outline.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Jordan - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Jordanian chevrons are white with red arrows.

--- NOTE:

You can use chevrons to distinguish between Jordan and Israel:

  • The Israeli chevrons are black with white arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/jordan.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Chevrons
metas.note: • Unlike neighbouring countries, Kazakhstan primarily uses yellow and black chevrons, except on T Intersections, where you will find the more generic red and white chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Latvia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Latvia uses white chevrons with red arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Many other European countries, including Lithuania and Poland, use the same chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/latvia.

metas.name: Lithuania - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Lithuania uses white chevrons with red arrows.
  • The small single chevrons (pictured here) usually have a red outline on the edge of the sign.

--- NOTE:

  • Many other European countries, including Latvia and Poland, use the same chevrons (though without the red outline).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lithuania.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Chevrons are black with yellow arrows.
  • You may also rarely come across blue and yellow chevrons.

--- NOTE:

  • None of Luxembourg’s neighbours use these chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/luxembourg.

metas.name: Madeira - Chevrons
metas.note: • Since Madeira is an autonomous region of Portugal, you will often come across various types of Portuguese infrastructure, such as poles and chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Montenegro - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Montenegro uses black on white or red on yellow chevrons.

--- NOTE:

  • Albania uses white on black chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/montenegro.

metas.name: New Zealand - Chevrons
metas.note:
• New Zealand uses black-on-yellow chevrons with a thin black border.
  • White on black chevrons are very rarely used.

--- NOTE:

  • Australia’s chevrons have the same colours, but do not have the border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Norway - Chevrons
metas.note: • Norway uses yellow on black chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Oman - Chevrons
metas.note: • Oman uses black-and-yellow chevrons that have an unusually large number of arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/oman.

metas.name: Philippines - Chevrons
metas.note: • Chevrons are typically red on white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Poland - Chevrons
metas.note: • Polish chevrons are white with red arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/poland.

metas.name: Portugal - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Portuguese chevrons are black with yellow arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Portugal is the only Mediterranean country with this chevron colour scheme.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Qatar - Chevrons
metas.note: • Qatar uses white on red and white on blue chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/qatar.

metas.name: Romania - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Romanian chevrons are red on white, often with a yellow frame.

--- NOTE:

  • Several eastern and central European countries have the red on white chevrons, however yellow frames are by far the most common in Romania.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/romania.

metas.name: San Marino - Chevrons
metas.note: • San Marino uses yellow chevrons with burgundy red arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/san-marino.

metas.name: Serbia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Serbia uses chevrons with a black arrow on a white background.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Europe, these chevrons can also be found in Slovenia, Montenegro and North Macedonia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/serbia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Slovak and Czech chevrons are white with red arrows.
  • Less commonly, you may find red on yellow chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovenia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Slovenian chevrons usually have red arrows on a white background.
  • You can also find a less common version with a black arrow on a white background.

--- NOTE:

  • Austrian chevrons are either white on red or red on yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovenia.

metas.name: South Africa - Chevrons
metas.note:
• South Africa uses white-and-red chevrons.
  • In addition, unique-looking small, thin chevrons with one arrow are common next to roads.

--- NOTE:

  • The thin chevrons can also be found in the other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, and Lesotho.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: Spain - Chevrons
metas.note:
Spain has two chevrons:

  • Black with white arrows.
  • Blue with white arrows.
  • Chevrons with a single arrow are rare.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southern Europe, black with white chevrons can be found in Italy, Greece and Albania.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Sweden - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Sweden is the only country in Europe whose chevrons have yellow arrows on a blue background.

--- NOTE:

  • While very rare, yellow on blue chevrons also exist in Luxembourg.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Switzerland - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Chevrons are black with a white arrow.
  • You may also rarely find chevrons that are white with a black arrow.

--- NOTE:

  • Austrian chevrons are red and white, or red and yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/switzerland.

metas.name: Taiwan - Chevrons
metas.note: • Taiwan uses black on yellow chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Turkey - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Turkish chevrons are typically red on white.
  • Beware that there are some other regional variants.
  • Usually, the tip of the arrow does not touch the edge of the chevron.
  • Some chevrons have a neon yellow border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Intersection Chevrons
metas.note: • On intersections, you can often find this distinctive black and yellow chevron, with multiple arrows that point upward.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Ukraine - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Ukraine uses a red chevron with white arrows.
  • Russia and Estonia use the same chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ukraine.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Chevrons are black with white arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Irish chevrons are black with yellow arrows.
  • French chevrons are blue with white arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: Uruguay - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Like most of Latin America, chevrons are yellow with black arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mostly useful to distinguish between Argentina, which uniquely uses chevrons that are white with red arrows.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.
